faq.a1: Yes. There are no ads, no fees and no paid version. It is made by students of The Skyward Project.
faq.a2: Only the first time, to load the app and its reading tools. After that, most of Saath works without a connection.
faq.q3: Can it read Hindi or Marathi papers?
faq.a3: Yes. It reads printed papers in English, Hindi and Marathi. Handwriting is harder, so always check the numbers it finds.
faq.q4: What if my phone can’t speak my language?
faq.a4: Some phones don’t have a Hindi or Marathi voice. Saath will tell you, and you can still read everything on screen.
faq.q5: Will Saath tell me whether to take a loan?
faq.a5: No. Saath explains what the paper says and what it really costs. The choice is yours. Talk to someone you trust before you sign.

partners.title: Privacy for teachers and partners
partners.b1: Saath has no accounts and no server of its own. Each student's nickname, optional school code and grade, tracker entries, lesson and path progress, drill results and FinLit Check results are stored in that phone's browser storage. A PIN, if set, is stored only as a salted hash.
partners.b2: Scanned documents, photos, the text read from them, tracked loans, tracker entries, the nickname, the PIN and individual answers. Saath collects no real names, phone numbers, emails, locations or device identifiers, and has no analytics, advertising or behavioural profiling.
partners.b3: A student who has joined a school can switch on sharing. It is off by default. When it is on, and only if this deployment has an endpoint configured, Saath sends small anonymous events: the school code, the grade, the kind of event (joined, a FinLit Check before or after, a lesson or path finished) and, for a check, four unit scores. No name, nickname or device identifier is included.
partners.b4: The partner view shows totals for a school and grade: students joined, lessons and paths finished, and the average change per unit between the first and second FinLit Check. It never shows an individual student, and any group smaller than ten is hidden.
partners.b5: “Delete everything on this phone” in the profile removes all local data. Anonymous events already sent cannot be traced back to a student, so they cannot be picked out and removed.
partners.b6: Saath is used by minors. Before any cloud sync, account system or new data collection is added, a qualified person must review it against India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, including the rules on children's data and verifiable parental consent.
